messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache paging spike detected in prod across us-west-2-GPUs — sustained growth in active pages. Auto-mitigation triggered: continuous-batch backoff active.

Alice H.: seeing it on dashboards, tailing logs now. RTT p50 jumped from 28ms -> 220ms for text-gen routes.

Mike L.: paging rate up 6x in last 3min, eviction churn high. KV cache resident set increased by 42%.

Sara R.: streaming token cadence showing stalls — clients observe long pauses ~1.2s between token bursts. Might be partial flush that we patched last month?

Alice H.: right, this smells like the recent batching throttle change interacting with prefetch paging. If prefix cache misses spike, continuous batching grows batch size and we hit memory/paging cliff.

TJ: oncall here, taking ownership. First actions: 1) pin batch_size to safe value, 2) disable aggressive prefetch on canary hosts, 3) roll a config hotfix.

Infra Bot: runbook check: CONFIG_ROLLOUT -> patch config key `continuous.batch_max_tokens` from 4096 -> 1024, `prefetch.enabled` -> false on affected pool.

Alice H.: good. I'll push the config change to staging then canary. command: ```rctl config set --env prod --pool us-west-2-gpu continuous.batch_max_tokens=1024 prefetch.enabled=false --reason "mitigate paging spike"```

Mike L.: I'm going to scale up eviction throttle to reduce churn while we let cache settle: `kvctl set eviction_rate=0.6` on nodegroup-3

Sara R.: deploying the config to 10% canary now. Watching tok cadence in realtime.

(Oncall Bot): Deploy started by Alice H. — canary hosts: cg-45,cg-46, expected completion 60s.

Alice H.: canary patched. Observing p50 latency dip back to ~70ms, paging rate on canary down 80%. Token cadence still showing small micro-stalls but much reduced.

Mike L.: rolling to 50% now. I've also throttled non-tenant-critical background prefetch jobs: `jobsctl pause prefetch-backfill --match "low-prio"`

Karen (Customer Success): FYI — a handful of premium customers reported timeouts on chat endpoints ~18:03-18:10. CS is triaging support tickets. We'll prepare an incident update.

TJ: good note. Impact assessment: error rate on chat endpoints peaked at 4.7% (from 0.1%), median latency up 6x. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/generate. No data loss detected.

Infra Bot: Rolling to 100% in progress. Estimated time to finish: 3m.

Mike L.: config fully rolled out across us-west-2-pool. Eviction rate adjustment in place. Paging metrics trending down but there's a residual periodic cadence stall every ~90s likely due to KV compaction cycles.

Sara R.: I see a partial flush pattern in logs correlated with compaction heartbeat: `kv_cache: partial_flush triggered shards=12 reason=compaction_padding` — that aligns with token cadence stall.

Alice H.: immediate mitigation viable: disable compaction-triggered partial flushes for the window. Command: `kvctl set compaction.partial_flush_enabled=false --scope pool:us-west-2`

TJ: apply that, and keep compaction manual for the next 2 hours. Also enable our fallback policy: route streaming requests to low-latency variant model (model-v2-small) for heavy tenants until stable.

Alice H.: compaction partial flush disabled. Fallback routing enabled for tiered-tenants via policy `route-policy:stream-fallback` (applied).

Mike L.: after compaction disable, token cadence stalls disappeared in the next sampling window. p95 latency for streaming dropped from 1.8s -> 320ms.

Karen (Customer Success): sending customer note template to CS channel now. Will include ETA and mitigation steps.

TJ: summary for handoff — root cause hypothesis: interaction between recent continuous-batching config and KV cache compaction/prefetch that created a feedback loop (miss -> bigger batches -> memory pressure -> paging -> compaction -> partial flush -> token cadence stalls). Mitigations applied: reduced batch_max_tokens, disabled prefetch, raised eviction throttle, disabled compaction-triggered partial flush, enabled model fallback for streaming, rolled config to 100%.

Alice H.: logs and metrics snapshots uploaded to incident page https://redwood.in/incident/2645012345, include tracer spans for three example requests.

Oncall Bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Postmortem required: severity P2 (customer impact: transient timeouts for premium customers, degraded latency).

TJ: handing off to Mike L. for next 2 hours of monitoring and postmortem drafting. Mike — if anything regresses, escalate to Eng-Infra and Eng-ML.

Mike L.: taking handoff. I'll keep watch on paging, eviction, and token cadence dashboards and loop in Eng-ML for compaction logic review.

Sara R.: I'll start collecting prompt/eval sets that triggered the largest cache churn for the PM/ML review.

Karen (Customer Success): I'll send an updated customer-facing message in 30m with mitigation summary and next steps.

TJ: thanks all. Closing thread for active ops — keep logging here if anything new pops. :thumbsup:
